newsitem.title: MOZAMBIQUE: Old Mozambique war foe threatens to march in Maputo.
newsitem.headline: Old Mozambique war foe threatens to march in Maputo.

text.p: The leader of Mozambique's National Resistance Movement, Renamo, warned that the wave of demonstrations against its former enemy in war, the ruling Frelimo Party, would spread to the capital Maputo.

Renamo party chief Afonso Dhlakama was reported in Wednesday's Maputo daily Noticias as saying his supporters would march on President Joaquim Chissano's office to show their discontent with the high cost of living and with what he called bad government.
He said that as leader of the biggest opposition party in parliament he might join the demonstrations.

"Throughout the world opposition leaders head peaceful demonstrations ... Why can't I be at the head of a demonstration? I'm not afraid of anything, and if Frelimo wants, let them kill me with their police," he said.
Renamo waged a 16-year war against Frelimo, only to lose parliamentary and presidential elections in 1994, which were judged free and fair by United Nations observers.
Since May 5 Renamo has staged several street protests in the centre and north of the country, which have been dispersed by police who have arrested about 60 people.

The government has ruled the demonstrations illegal in terms of a 1991 law which states organisers must give the authorities details of the time, venue and place of a public demonstration at least four working days in advance.
Dhlakama warned against trials for those arrested.
"Nobody's going to court. There is no way that Renamo would accept trials of the protesters," he said.
Dhlakama added that the use of force by the police against protesters meant that Frelimo had "declared war against Renamo and against the public".
He said protests in Maputo would also focus on the "disastrous" performance of parliament.
He said at its last session, which ran from mid-February to the end of April, parliament rejected all the major amendments moved by Renamo to the government's local authority legislation.
